title: Derived-unit normalization without a spectral edge
statement: Let B be Grothendieck abelian, C abelian, both with derived categories, G additive left exact, L a bounded below integer-indexed cochain complex, and n ∈ ℕ. Assume L^i is zero for i ≠ n. Put X = H^n(Q L) and T = G L. Let f : Q L → X[n] induce the identity under the canonical H^n(X[n]) ≅ X. For any a : G(Z^n L) → Z^n T with a i_T = G(i_L), the composite a, the homology projection of T, the inverse quotient homology comparison, H^n of the derived unit, H^n(RG f), and [def-pc-right-derived-single-degree-comparison] equals G of the homology projection of L followed by the inverse quotient homology comparison. This lemma has no truncation, spectral object, spectral edge, or extension-by-zero map.

source.place: Proof, remark (1), and single-complex specialization; canonical comparison elaborated by A3.

proof.text: The support assumption gives a concrete isomorphism L ≅ L^n[n]. Shift by n and commute the derived unit with the shift. The given normalization on f identifies it with the canonical single-degree identification, by faithfulness of homology between pure degree-n objects. Use the quotient homology comparisons to express its cycle representative.

Shift to degree zero using NatTrans.CommShift for the derived unit and the single-functor and homology shift isomorphisms. The composite becomes rightDerivedPlusSingleUnitHomology followed by its single-complex comparison. Apply the already proved rightDerivedPlusSingleUnitHomology_comp_comparison to obtain toRightDerivedZero. For left exact G this is rightDerivedZeroIsoSelf.inv, so composing its hom gives the identity. Transport back through the quotient and shift comparisons; uniqueness of a by the mono cycle inclusion identifies its representative. This includes n=0 and a zero coefficient.

lean.statement:
theorem rightDerivedFunctorPlusUnit_single_degree
    (L : CochainComplex.Plus B) (n : ℕ)
    (hL : ∀ i : ℤ, i ≠ (n : ℤ) → IsZero (L.obj.X i)) :
    let T := (G.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj L.obj
    let GL := G.mapCochainComplexPlus.obj L
    let X := (DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor B n).obj (DerivedCategory.Plus.Q.obj L)
    ∀ (f : DerivedCategory.Plus.Q.obj L ⟶ (DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor B n).obj X),
      (DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor B n).map f ≫
        (DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctorCompHomologyFunctorIso (C := B) n).hom.app X =
          𝟙 X →
      ∀ (a : G.obj (L.obj.cycles n) ⟶ T.cycles n),
        a ≫ T.iCycles n = G.map (L.obj.iCycles n) →
      a ≫ T.homologyπ n ≫
          (DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctorObjQIso GL n).inv ≫
          (DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor C n).map
            (G.rightDerivedFunctorPlusUnit.app ((HomotopyCategory.Plus.quotient B).obj L)) ≫
          (DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor C n).map (G.rightDerivedFunctorPlus.map f) ≫
          (G.rightDerivedSingleDegreeComparison n).hom.app X =
        G.map (L.obj.homologyπ n ≫
          (DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctorObjQIso L n).inv)
